principles.name: Interface First
principles.summary: Design the agent interface before any human UI. Tool definitions are the first artifact of every feature — regardless of whether you ship them as MCP, CLI, SDK, or function specs.

principles.name: Contract First
principles.summary: Write usage rules — permissions, constraints, sequences, formatting — before implementation. Without them, agents hallucinate identifiers and violate constraints.

principles.name: Prep Gates
principles.summary: Validate credentials, load fresh IDs, and confirm system health before every session. Stale context is the #1 source of agent errors.

principles.name: Typed State
principles.summary: All persistent agent state flows through a single structured data contract with versioned migrations. Each module owns its slice.

principles.name: Visible Outputs
principles.summary: Agent actions produce human-readable results in existing workflow tools (Slack, email, task manager) — not a JSON blob in a dashboard nobody opens.

principles.name: Multi-Model Verification
principles.summary: High-stakes decisions fan out to multiple models. Trust agreement. A finding three models flag is almost certainly real; one model alone is a hypothesis.

principles.name: Perspective Dispatch
principles.summary: Complex reviews dispatch multiple constrained perspectives (security, UX, new-user, performance) against the same artifact. Each persona has a defined focus area.

principles.name: Autonomous Recovery
principles.summary: The system retries with backoff before alerting. Humans only get pulled in when self-healing has already failed — and the alert includes what happened, what was tried, and a direct link to take manual action.

principles.name: Inspectable State
principles.summary: Every agent server exposes its own operational state — queue depth, throughput, recent activity, trends, health — via a typed agent tool, not just a human dashboard. The complement to Visible Outputs: results to humans where they already are, system state to agents where they already are. Where Prep Gates answers 'is the system READY?', Inspectable State answers 'what is the STATE of the work?'.

adoption_levels.name: No agent access
adoption_levels.marker: Human operates all tools through UIs

adoption_levels.name: Agent as Afterthought
adoption_levels.marker: Thin API wrappers; no contracts, no validation

adoption_levels.name: Agent-Aware
adoption_levels.marker: Usage rules exist; state is typed; pre-flight checks validate before use

adoption_levels.name: Agents First
adoption_levels.marker: Agent interface designed and shipped first; agent is primary consumer

adoption_levels.name: Agent-Driven
adoption_levels.marker: Agents extend the system for other agents; self-healing; multi-model checks
